How to Use MAT Codex

MAT can be read at several levels.

Level 1 — Human Reference

Open a numbered MAT record and read it as a scientific reference entry.

The main Markdown record provides the human-readable description.

Level 2 — Detailed Scientific Data

Follow tables and data files associated with the record.

These contain individual measurements, units, conditions, uncertainties and evidence information.

Level 3 — Relationships

Follow identifiers linking a record to:

  • isotopes;
  • compounds;
  • materials;
  • processes;
  • environments;
  • experiments;
  • sources;
  • applications.

Level 4 — Visualisation

Each record may contain associated:

  • images;
  • diagrams;
  • graphs;
  • plots;
  • tables;
  • three-dimensional models;
  • spectral visualisations;
  • field visualisations.

Visual assets must reference the data from which they were produced whenever applicable.

Level 5 — Machine Processing

Structured MAT data may eventually be processed computationally for:

  • comparison;
  • filtering;
  • graph traversal;
  • simulation input;
  • statistical analysis;
  • optimisation;
  • machine learning;
  • materials discovery.

Reading Evidence

A value should never be interpreted without considering its evidence status.

The reader should distinguish between:

  • measured;
  • independently reproduced;
  • theoretically calculated;
  • computationally predicted;
  • experimental;
  • historical;
  • hypothetical;
  • unverified.

See:

docs/02-data/05-Evidence-and-Provenance.md

Imported research — review pending. Recovered from 42.txt, line 987. Source assertions of validation are historical statements, not independent test results. See the intake ledger for duplicates and unresolved references.

CALC-003 — Sodium-24 Beta-Minus Decay

$$ {}^{24}Na \rightarrow {}^{24}Mg+e^-+\bar\nu_e $$

Atomic masses:

$$ M({}^{24}Na)=23.990962950\ u $$
$$ M({}^{24}Mg)=23.985041697\ u $$

For β⁻ decay:

$$ Q_{\beta^-} = [M_p-M_d]c^2 $$
$$ \boxed{ Q_{\beta^-}\approx5.51561\ {\rm MeV} } $$

This total Q value must not be confused with the electron endpoint for a particular branch because much of the decay proceeds through excited ²⁴Mg levels followed by gamma emission.

Related spectroscopy and liquid-state research notes.

Magnesium — Evaluated Nuclear States

MAT Core Data · dated evaluation. 28 nuclear states are transcribed from NUBASE2020, published in 2021. This is a reproducible source extraction, not independent experimental validation or a claim that later research is complete.

  • Parent Magnesium record
  • Structured evaluation
  • Retained original source
  • Evaluation paper · SRC-000008

How to read this table

A is the mass number; N is the neutron count. Ground states, isomers, levels and isobaric analogue states retain the source state index. Mass excess is in keV, not atomic mass units. A # means an estimate from systematics; ?, inequalities, asymmetric uncertainty text and spin qualifiers are preserved. stbl means stable in this evaluation, p-unst means particle unstable. Blank source fields remain unavailable. The final column preserves decay/abundance notation without equating decay branching with natural abundance.
